sheet-1.description: Sheet 75 of the New Jersey Coast volume 1 covers the centre of the village of Little Silver at 60 ft to an inch, drawn with north towards the upper left. Rumson Road runs up the left third of the sheet and Church Street crosses the sheet diagonally; Prospect Avenue runs along the bottom between them and continues to the east, and Parker Avenue (today Harrison Avenue) leaves Rumson Road to the west near the top. A narrow unnamed lane, 17 ft wide at Rumson Road and 25 ft at Church Street (today Church Lane), links the two roads in the middle of the sheet. The village is thinly built: detached dwellings on large lots, a few sheds and barns, and small commercial buildings near the lane, among them a meat and grocery store, a hall, and the W. H. Carhart wagon shop with a blacksmith, a wheelwright and the hand engine house of the fire department on Rumson Road. Most of the block east of Church Street is taken by the J. T. Lovett Co. green houses, long glass-roofed ranges with store houses, an office, an ice house, a heater and a water tank on a 20 ft elevation. A large cemetery fills the block between Rumson Road and Church Street, with the M. E. Church on its Church Street side; a post office and store stands opposite. A public school, a grocery and a blacksmith shop face Prospect Avenue at the bottom of the sheet. The title block gives the population as 500, says there is no steam engine, one hand engine and 500 ft of hose, and refers water facilities to the Long Branch report.
notes: Parker Av. is today Harrison Avenue (OpenStreetMap); Parker Avenue today is a different street south of the village.
The unnamed lane between Rumson Road and Church Street is today Church Lane; it is drawn 17 ft wide at Rumson Road and 25 ft at Church Street.
Church is lettered without a suffix; today Church Street.
Prospect Av. is drawn 40 ft wide west of Church and 50 to 55 ft east of it.
Water facilities are referred to the Long Branch report.
Dated M.J. 3.8.07 in the lower right corner.

sheet-2-1.description: The lower part of sheet 76 of the New Jersey Coast volume 1 shows Little Silver Point, printed as 1 3/4 miles north-east of the Little Silver depot, at 60 ft to an inch with north at the top. Point Road crosses the part from west to east, 40 to 47 ft wide, bending slightly where it straightens out to the east, and a lane (today Borden Place) leaves it to the south at the left edge of the sheet. North of the road the lots run down to the shore of the North Branch of South Shrewsbury River, drawn in blue across the top of the part, with a pier built on piles reaching out into the river near the right edge. The point is a summer resort: a hotel at the left edge, Hotel Pontin to the right, and a few large detached dwellings with stables and a store house on the river lots, one with a wind mill and water tank. South of the road the lots are deep and nearly empty, with a few dwellings, outbuildings and a wind mill with a tank; a narrow 42 ft lot runs south from the road between lots 29 and 31, and a diagonal back line closes the lots at the bottom of the sheet. The rest of the paper below that line is blank. The compass rose and the scale bar are drawn in the lower right corner. The two upper parts of the sheet, separated by a heavy line, show outlying works away from the village and are not part of this annotation.
notes: Point R'd is today Little Silver Point Road; the lane at the left edge is today Borden Place.
The north arrow appears to point to magnetic north: the fit puts true north about 3 degrees left of straight up, the arrow about 12 degrees.
Placed from three points along Point Road (Borden Place junction, the bend in the road, and a modern driveway at the narrow lot 30); position across the road is better determined than rotation.
Hotel Pontin; a pier built on piles.

Printed sheet 76: three parts. Top left: E.C. Hazard & Co grocery-specialties works, '3/4 Mile W of Little Silver Depot', no street drawn; top right: House of the Holy Angel, '1/2 Mile S.E. of Little Silver Depot', no street drawn; bottom: Little Silver Point, Point Rd (now Little Silver Point Road) along the North Branch of South Shrewsbury River, 'Lane' at the left edge (now Borden Place).
